newsitem.title: UK: Latam, E.Europe top emerging market picks - survey.
newsitem.headline: Latam, E.Europe top emerging market picks - survey.

text.p: Institutional investors in emerging market equities expect good growth in Latin America and eastern Europe and a return to market growth in most Asian markets, a survey released on Monday showed.
The quarterly survey, by consultants Burston Marsteller, said Latin America and eastern Europe were viewed more positively than Asia Pacific, with southern Europe attracting renewed interest.

"Key themes for emerging markets in the next 12 months include attractive valuations, low interest rates, good liquidity and continuing privatisation," said the survey, which covered institutions managing 85 percent by value of the world's global emerging market funds.
It said investors would watch U.S. interest rates but felt only a slight increase was likely and thus would not impact badly on emerging markets.
The report said South East Asia was experiencing a comeback supported by the strengthening of the yen against the dollar, which had increased the competitiveness of the region's exporters.

"(But) the slight shift in favour of Asia should not be overestimated," it warned. It said Indonesia was one of the most attractive markets in the region, but Malaysia attracted mixed responses, with some fund managers expressing concern that it could face the same difficulties experienced by Thailand.
Managers also felt Thailand may not have hit bottom and still suffered structural problems and an overvalued baht.
It said eastern Europe offered good opportunities but valuations were seen becoming expensive. Hungary and Poland are preferred to the Czech Republic.
In Latin America, Brazil and Mexico are preferred but Chile is widely held to be the region's long-term success story.
Fund managers were showing increased interest in Middle Eastern and North African markets because of new issues and privatisations.
